title: Adoption by any product
statement: Teams beyond Lathe's own come to know their products the same way: each adopts Lathe in its own repo, fits it to the kinds its product needs without forking it, and keeps relying on it as the product grows large.
measure: The product repos outside this one whose `lathe check` runs on the published package with its schema unchanged, counted from the installs the Owner knows of; and, for specs about ten times Lathe's own size, whether an edit still shows within the Platform performance budgets.
target: At least two such product repos, none with a forked schema, within six months of the first published release; at ten times Lathe's size, an edit visible within 500 ms and checks within 4 s.
measured_outside: The Owner counts the product repos outside this one whose `lathe check` runs on the published package, from the installs they know of, and looks in each for a schema of its own; no test or record in this repo can see another repo. The size part is measured in this repo by the performance suite on the large synthetic product.
notes: Serves LA-BO11 for products other than Lathe: the headline holds only if any product can be known this way, not Lathe alone. LA-JR02 (Bring a product onto Lathe) is how each one adopts it, and LA-JR03 (Move a product to a new Lathe) how it keeps up; this outcome counts them, untimed.

title: Agents held to spec
statement: Agents are held to what the Owner decided: an Agent builds from the spec's records, a wrong write is refused and the rest is checked, so its change matches the use cases, rules and tests it was given and merges without being sent back, with no policing by the Owner.
measure: The share of an Agent's changes built from the spec that merge into main without rework (no send-back for a missed requirement or rule, and no fix-up commit on the same work before it merges), counted each month from the merges the Owner reviews. Second, hand-written accidental code: the share of Lathe's accidental records (its technical records and engineering standards) that are hand-written fills of a pattern's slot or that nothing accounts for, read from Lathe's own check, which lists each domain's accidental debt and warns of each accidental record nothing accounts for.
target: At least 80% within three months of the first published release, and 90% within a year. Hand-written accidental code shrinks: under 20% of Lathe's accidental records are fills or unaccounted for by 2027-06-30.
measured_outside: The Owner tallies each month, from the branches they review and merge, which of an Agent's changes merged as first handed in and which were sent back or needed a fix-up for something the spec said; no test in this repo sees the review.
notes: The enforcement outcome beside the headline LA-BO11: decided once and held to it is what makes the Owner's understanding trustworthy, since the records are what was built. LA-JR01 (Take an idea to proof) shows it: the Agent builds from the records, a wrong write is refused and the check catches what is left before the Owner reviews. LA-JR04 (Change something on purpose) ends in merges this outcome counts too.

title: Status from the spec
statement: The Owner learns what is built, proved or still missing from the spec itself, without asking an Agent.
measure: The status questions the Owner still has to ask an Agent each week (what is done, what is tested, what is left) because the spec and its coverage could not answer them, and the coverage claims (designed, built or proved) the Owner finds false on review.
target: At most one such question a week, and no coverage claim found false, within three months of the first published release.
measured_outside: The Owner keeps a weekly tally of the status questions they ask Agents that the spec could not answer, and, for each branch they review, of the records coverage calls designed, built or proved whose claim the code or tests show false (built with nothing implementing it, proved by a test that does not prove it); `lathe check` prints the coverage they compare.
notes: Serves LA-BO11: knowing what is built, proved and missing is the Owner's view of the whole product, where the headline asks about one part. LA-JR06 (See where the product stands) is the moment it counts: each status question that journey leaves unanswered is one the Owner asks an Agent.

title: Mistakes stopped before main
statement: Agents are held to the spec's requirements and rules before their work merges: a mistake one of them would catch is refused or found by the check, not found later on main.
measure: Defects found on main after a merge that a requirement, rule or test written in the spec would have caught, counted per month.
target: At most one a month, within six months of the first published release.
measured_outside: The Owner records each defect found on main after a merge and judges whether a requirement, rule or test in the spec would have caught it, counting them each month from the fixes they merge.
notes: Serves LA-BO11 beside LA-BO06: a mistake stopped before it merges is a break that never happens by accident. LA-JR01 (Take an idea to proof) and LA-JR04 (Change something on purpose) are where the refusals, the check and the Owner's review catch it; this outcome counts what got past them.

title: Quick idea to proof
statement: A new piece of behavior the Owner decides on is built and proved quickly, by Agents, without the Owner writing its code.
measure: The median days from the commit that first adds a use case to the commit in which its flow test and every one of its use case tests are automated and their files name their IDs, over the use cases added each month.
target: A median under two days, within six months of the first published release.
measured_outside: The Owner takes both dates from git for each use case added in the month: the commit that first adds it, and the first commit on main in which its flow test and every use case test under it are automated and their files name their IDs (Lathe records no test run, so this is the closest proof the history holds); and works out the median each month.
notes: Serves LA-BO11: directing rather than coding only pays when what the Owner decides is built and proved quickly. LA-JR01 (Take an idea to proof) is the journey its measure times, from the use case written to its tests automated.

title: Newcomers understand quickly
statement: Someone meeting a product for the first time, an Agent or a Reader, understands a part of it quickly: given a requirement, they find what builds and proves it, and a Reader on a phone finds a record and reads it as readily as at a desk.
measure: The time a new Agent or Reader takes to find the code and the tests behind a requirement they are given, timed in a short trial on a product they have not seen. Second, on a phone: the time a Reader takes, from opening the app on a phone, to find a named record and read its statement, timed in the same kind of trial.
target: Under five minutes, median over the trials, within three months of the first published release. On a phone, under 30 seconds, median over the trials, by 2027-03-31.
measured_outside: The Owner runs the trial with each new Agent or Reader: names a requirement, times how long it takes them to name its code file and its tests, and keeps the median. For the phone measure the Owner names a record to a Reader holding a phone with the app open, times until they read its statement aloud, and keeps the median.
notes: Serves LA-BO11 for someone new: the headline's question of what proves a part, asked by an Agent or a Reader who has not seen the product. LA-JR05 (Answer why something exists) is the moment its trial times, at a desk and on a phone.

title: Understood better than built
statement: The Owner, who directs while Agents build, understands the product better than if they had written its code themselves: for any part of it they can say why it exists, what proves it and what a change to it would touch, from Lathe alone, so no change breaks something by accident.
measure: Of the questions the Owner asks about a part of the product (why it exists, what proves it, what a change to it would touch), the share answered from Lathe alone, without asking an Agent or reading the code or its history, and the median minutes to answer one, tallied each week. Second, the accidental breaks: things a merged change broke that the Owner did not see it would touch before it was made, counted per month.
target: At least 90% answered from Lathe alone, a median under two minutes, and no accidental break in a month, within six months of the first published release.
measured_outside: The Owner keeps a weekly tally of the questions they ask about a part of the product, noting for each whether Lathe alone answered it and how many minutes it took, and works out the share and the median. For each break found after a merge, they note whether they saw beforehand that the change would touch it; a break they did not see counts as accidental.
notes: The headline outcome: what Lathe is for, the product understood better than by those who built it. It is kept to understanding, and LA-BO06 (Agents held to spec) stands beside it as the enforcement outcome, because decided once and held to it are what make the understanding trustworthy, and naming them here would repeat LA-BO06's and LA-BO08's measures. The others each serve it: LA-BO07 is its question of status, LA-BO10 its question of what proves a part, for someone new; LA-BO08 and LA-BO09 are what holding Agents to the spec buys; LA-BO05 is the same for other products. The journeys LA-JR04 (Change something on purpose) and LA-JR05 (Answer why something exists) are the moments its measure counts.
